title: Keep the names
hook: good, modest, truthful, even-minded: keep these names and deserve them (Meditations 10.8)

segments.voice: Yesterday: formed to bear it. Your line was made to bear it. Which part of the weight turned out to be the story? Day six hundred fifteen.

A name tag at a conference. A title in an email signature. Mom, coach, nurse, friend. Names do work: they tell people what to expect from us, and they quietly tell us what to expect from ourselves. In book ten Marcus picks out a short list of names he wants to answer to, and then he tells himself something harder. Don't just wear them. Deserve them. Today: keep the names.
screen: `A NAME TAG.` → `NAMES DO WORK.` → `KEEP THE NAMES.`

segments.voice: First, the list. Once you've taken these names, Marcus writes, good, modest, truthful, rational, even-minded, high-minded, take care not to trade them for others. And if you lose them, come back to them quickly. Second, the meanings. He defines three of them. Rational means paying attention: looking at each thing carefully, not carelessly. Even-minded means accepting willingly what the nature of the whole hands you. High-minded means lifting your mind above the body's pleasures and pains, above shabby fame, and above death. Third, not for praise. Hold on to the names, he says, without wanting other people to call you by them. A name you live by is different from a name you're given. The coach who's called coach but never shows up has the name and not the thing. Fourth, a hard picture. Clinging to life without these names, Marcus says, is like the fighters in the arena, half eaten by wild beasts, covered in wounds and blood, still begging to be kept until tomorrow, only to be thrown again to the same claws. It's a brutal image, and he turns it on himself: better to be these few names truly than to be many things badly. And if you feel yourself slipping, he says, go off to some quiet corner where you can hold on to them again.
screen: `SIX NAMES TO TAKE.` · `ATTENTIVE, ACCEPTING, LIFTED.` · `LIVED, NOT CALLED.` · `THE ARENA, AND THE QUIET CORNER.` · then, large: `KEEP THE NAME.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Hear the six names: good, modest, truthful, attentive, even-minded, high-minded. Let one of them stand out, the one you'd most like to deserve today. Don't pick the one you're best at. Pick the one you need. Now picture one moment ahead where you'll need it: a meeting, a conversation, a temptation. See yourself answering to that name there. The bell holds the time.
Keep the names. Marcus's short list: good, modest, truthful, rational, even-minded, high-minded. Not to be called them, but to deserve them. Today's word.
Your line: keep the name. Pick one of the six and live it on purpose today. If you slip, come back to it quickly. Day six hundred fifteen.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Meditations choose one of Marcus's names each morning, truthful or even-minded, say, and return to it during the day whenever they notice they've let it slip.

original.note: Greek: a name. Marcus asks himself to keep a few names, and deserve them.

trapdoor: what you thought: a list of nice adjectives.
what it means: six names to live by, not to be called by; when you lose one, come back.
what a scholar hears: the passage pairs the names with a harsh arena image, fighters half eaten by beasts who still beg for another day, a picture of clinging to life without character.

notes: 10.8 paraphrased: the names (Long: good, modest, true, rational, a man of equanimity, magnanimous); the definitions of rational, equanimity, magnanimity; 'without desiring to be called by these names by others'; the half-devoured arena fighters; 'betake thyself to some nook where thou shalt maintain them'. Confirm.
